issues.issue: Did the officer unreasonably assess the psychological evidence, contrary to Kanthasamy?
issues.applicant_position: Officer's psychological-evidence analysis mirrors the unreasonable approach in Kanthasamy, demanding proof of treatment and availability.
issues.respondent_position: Officer may implicitly have concluded that return to Pakistan would remove the uncertainty causing the symptoms.
issues.result_quote: I therefore conclude that the officer’s evaluation of the psychological evidence suffered from the same analytical shortcomings that were found unreasonable in Kanthasamy.

issues.issue: Must the whole H&C decision be redetermined because of the unreasonable psychological analysis?
issues.applicant_position: Mental health was a material part of the H&C application, so the error requires redetermination.
issues.result_quote: The applicants’ H&C application must therefore be remitted for redetermination.

issues.issue: Were the hardship, establishment and best interests of the child findings unreasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Officer erred in assessing hardship in Pakistan, establishment in Canada and the best interests of the children.
issues.result_quote: As a result, I do not need to address the applicants’ other arguments related to the officer’s assessment of hardship
